title: Everything you asked for is done and live.
intro: Gab, every change from your sign-off is now in the Playbook: the course, three new lessons, re-recorded films, your facilitator guide and Ava. It's open to Ida and Marco, and to you and Jamie as managers.
release_note: Live from 14 October. The Playbook is open to Ida and Marco only; other trainers stay locked until Jamie opens it.
link_note: Lesson links open the Playbook after you sign in to the Trainer Portal.

live.title: What's live now
live.text: The updated course, three new lessons, 43 re-recorded or new films, your facilitator guide with printable observation sheets, Videos in this lesson, Review videos and Ava's updated knowledge. JF Coach and the Trainer Portal also stop trainers applying or publishing a program for a client on medical hold; you and Jamie can override as admins.

rows.title: Your price line is back
rows.changed: The script now uses the exact amount you asked for. The old last-intake urgency is gone; the client chooses their start week.

rows.title: High intent means both
rows.said: “High intent: sell the Kickstart and book a strategy session.”
rows.changed: Offer the Kickstart and, with the client’s agreement, book your 45-minute Strategy Session. You discuss ongoing prices. Discovery calls stay 15 minutes.
rows.quote: Sell the Kickstart AND, with their agreement, book Strategy.

rows.title: A hard no stays a no
rows.said: A hard no means no call, and JF Notes.
rows.changed: That is now the course guidance. If they are interested but unsure, offer your call and book it only with their agreement.
rows.quote: If it's a hard no, don't book a call. Add JF Notes with their words and contact preference.
rows.said_label: Your note, clarified by Jamie's ruling

rows.title: One current script to practise
rows.said: “A single current script practice sheet.” Add to course.
rows.changed: A new lesson brings the conversation, offer, five stages, booking, payment and outcome into one rehearsal.

rows.title: Two choices, with the reason
rows.said: “Two-choice scheduling and routine explanation.” Add to course.
rows.changed: Offer two workable times and explain how a routine helps. Different Kickstart session times are fine within the 21-day window from the chosen Monday.
rows.quote: Offer two times that fit the client's routine and your agreed hours. A regular day/time makes training easier to remember and protects diary space.

rows.title: Your five-stage method is taught and rehearsed
rows.changed: The course teaches the five stages and your shift guide keeps the rehearsal. Start at full price; offer a discount only after a genuine concern.

answer_groups.title: Coaching and the client’s first weeks

rows.title: Your weekly hard-set numbers
rows.changed: Per muscle each week, counting PT and solo training together. A compound set counts for its main muscles. These are adaptable defaults for recovery and ability.
rows.quote: Weekly hard sets per muscle: beginners 10–15; intermediate or advanced clients 8–12.

rows.title: Compound advice has your limit
rows.said: “Only for intermediate to advanced after assessment in the free session.”
rows.changed: The 5–10 reps and 2–3 minutes rest apply only to assessed intermediate or advanced clients. Beginner and isolation guidance stay as they were. The house effort guide still carries your name: leave 3–4 good reps for beginners and 1–3 for others.
rows.quote: For intermediate or advanced clients after assessment in the free session, compounds: 5–10 reps, 2–3 minutes rest.

rows.title: Week one starts with app confidence
rows.said: “App set up / demo, tracking meals.” Make sure they know the exercises and agree when they’ll do their next solo workout.
rows.changed: The new four-week lesson starts with familiar, safe exercises and agreeing when to do the next workout in Training. Week two covers nutrition and steps, week three independent training, and week four habits. Kickstart remains three sessions over 21 days.
rows.quote: Find the next solo workout in Training and agree when they’ll do it.

rows.title: Your food-support ladder
rows.said: “Meal guide → meal tracking → diary → scan.” Step down if there is resistance.
rows.changed: The course and shifts use your order when someone is resistant. Scan means the JF Coach photo food scan. Trainers check access without promising a price or inclusion.
rows.quote: meal guide → meal tracking → diary → scan

rows.title: Editing a workout, with a fresh check
rows.changed: The new lesson shows how to edit an existing workout, review and save it, then leave and reopen it to check. It applies from the next session; completed history stays as it was.
rows.quote: Leave the client’s page, reopen them in Programs and inspect Current program again.

rows.title: Advanced demos, warm-up sets and aids
rows.said: “Advanced demonstrations, warm-up-set progression and training aids.” Add to course.
rows.changed: The course adds safe demonstrations, gradual warm-up practice and familiar aids suited to the client. It does not invent a loading formula or a fixed aid list.
rows.quote: Check comfort and technique at each step; there is no universal set or loading formula.

rows.title: Stay with the client is prominent
rows.said: “Stay with the client must be highlighted.” “Keep both.”
rows.changed: Incident lessons now lead with staying with the client. Make the area safe, call 000 in an emergency, call you once help is underway, then keep both the call and JF Notes and file the same-day incident report.

rows.title: Your usual 1:1 guide is included
rows.said: “Build-up: 2x per week. Under 15 hours: 1x per week. 15+ hours: 1x per fortnight. 25+ hours: 1x coffee per month.”
rows.changed: The course and shift guide include your usual bands. Hours means weekly client hours. You still set each trainer’s actual cadence.
rows.quote: Build-up: 2x per week. Under 15 hours: 1x per week. 15+ hours: 1x per fortnight. 25+ hours: 1x coffee per month.

rows.title: Your shifts keep your discussion topics
rows.changed: All 23 topics are in your shift guide in your source wording, and each now sits inside a named block of its shift, so DiSC, the 6 Cs and the rest are covered within the four hours.
rows.quote: Each topic is discussed inside the block named on it, about five minutes, already within the 230 guided minutes.

rows.title: The outdated items are dropped
rows.said: Drop ClickUp. Drop the last-intake urgency.
rows.changed: ClickUp and the last-intake urgency are gone. The $149 comparison stays, as you asked in your selling notes, because Jamie confirmed it was the genuine former price.

new_tools.title: Your facilitator guide
new_tools.text: You said a guide with shift prompts would make it a 10 instead of a 5. Your guide gives each of your four four-hour online shifts: preparation, prompts in your words, demonstrations, practice and pass checks, with a 10-minute break. Open the Playbook Home and choose Facilitator guide.
steps: Choose “Print guide and observation sheet” in the guide, then print or save the pages as a PDF.
Print one reusable observation sheet for each trainer. It follows the four shift pages.
Lesson completion, setup, shift attendance, observed skills and final practical sign-off stay as separate records. Your printed ticks are not saved in the Playbook.
new_tools.extra: Confidence checks at shifts two and four carry into the first 1:1. Preparation follows whole chapters in the existing course order.

new_tools.title: The demo checklist
new_tools.link_label: Find the checklist in the guide
new_tools.text: The guide includes a short before-you-start checklist for the practice account, view, permitted action and reset plan.
steps: Use course simulations for free-session, Kickstart, Strategy and payment practice.
The staff demo is for ordinary 1:1 booking practice. Check the allowed action and reset limit before saving anything.
Keep notes as drafts until the note route is confirmed safe.
new_tools.extra: A demo label does not make every action safe.
new_tools.aria_label: Open Facilitator guide in the Playbook

new_tools.title: Videos in this lesson
new_tools.text: Each film now appears by title and actual length with a Watch button. Find the list under a lesson on the chapter page or expand it inside the lesson.
new_tools.extra: Watch opens a separate player. It does not mark the lesson or practice complete.

new_tools.title: Review videos
new_tools.text: Choose Review videos on the Playbook Home. Filter by chapter or lesson, search titles and transcripts, and jump to a spoken line.
new_tools.extra: This review view is for you and Jamie. Watching does not change course progress.

fixes.title: The voice glitches
fixes.text: Every voice glitch you heard is fixed, including the Ava Notes card. Films that repeated an old rule were re-voiced and re-recorded, and every new soundtrack was checked against its script, including another round on 14 October after a final audit.

fixes.title: One login and a working upload route
fixes.text: The Portal uses the same JF Coach email and password, and the lessons now say so. Missing certificates can be added through the signed-in Portal Credential upload or the original private email link.

fixes.title: The iPad wording
fixes.text: The lesson says to arrange iPad and JF towel delivery before the first client shift. The old promise of an in-person last-day handover is gone.

fixes.title: You teach online
fixes.text: The setup lessons match your online training. A club manager or named local mentor observes the rack safety bars, tape measurements and gym-floor walk in person. Equipment photos go to you privately; photos don't replace an observed skill check.

fixes.title: The held-client guard is live
fixes.text: JF Coach, Ava’s program actions and both Portal routes stop trainer apply, publish and live program changes while a medical hold is active. You and Jamie can override as admins. An override is not medical clearance to train.

fixes.title: Ava can help send client messages
fixes.text: Messaging is on. The course and Ava both say: check the exact client and draft, give an explicit yes, then check the JF Coach chat. Trainers can still send the message themselves.

fixes.title: Ava gives honest answers
fixes.text: Ava now separates feedback received from a change actually made. She needs proof before saying something was added or fixed, says when no published guide exists, and treats the old Levels checklists and forms as historical. She points managers to Trainer Portal More → Playbook → Facilitator guide.

fixes.title: Your late-move template
fixes.text: Ava now uses your exact wording for short-notice free-session move requests. It doesn't approve a booking change or send a message on its own.
fixes.quote: Normally there is a 12 hour notice period for rescheduling your appointment. However, as a one-off, we are happy to reschedule this one for you.

fixes.title: Clearer app reminders and records
fixes.text: The update explains the existing “Resend Kickstart form” button as a reminder to finish the app questionnaire. Lessons distinguish sessions done, booked and total, genuine past workout logs and flags that need checking.

fixes.title: Safer follow-through
fixes.text: The lessons add a 48-hour program check, goals and agreed next steps in outcomes, missed-call follow-up, agreed parent or payer involvement, and a personal message before a confirmed Strategy Session.

fixes.title: Program recovery and progress checks
fixes.text: The lessons show how to restore a saved program and reopen Training to check it. They clarify monthly repeats, both profiles in a shared booking, actual saved logs and an agreed measured baseline.

fixes.title: Practice questions match the changes
fixes.text: Quiz and practice questions follow your price line, Kickstart plus Strategy, the hard-set numbers, the stay-with-the-client order and Ava message approval. Band deadlifts are a regression or a home or hotel option, never the default for an advanced client.

fixes.title: Urgent texts start with URGENT
fixes.text: As you asked: routine and urgent non-emergency matters go to you by text, starting with URGENT so you can prioritise. Sick, running late, an injury or an incident is still a call, and 000 comes first in an emergency.

fixes.title: Free-session outcomes the same day
fixes.text: The outcome form is now due the same day, ideally straight after, with their goal, objections and the agreed next step. Other notes stay within 24 hours.

fixes.title: Your Kickstart script, in your words
fixes.text: The practice sheet now uses your script lines: the Jamie-mentioned opener (used only when true), your why and needs questions, the workout library, weekly messaging and habit coaching, “tap my phone” and the warm farewell with their name. Only the price line, the three-session package and the ruled call branches changed.

fixes.title: Repeats for 52 sessions
fixes.text: Ongoing clients with a regular time are booked to repeat weekly for 52 sessions (Repeat → Weekly, Ends → After N sessions), then the dates are checked.

fixes.title: Smaller things you raised
fixes.text: Your progression ladders and superset examples, the nickname or hidden-name choice, numbers as a shared support tool, gifted JF+ and the club desk-staff rewards (separate from trainer rewards) are now in the course.

fixes.title: Your guide, tightened
fixes.text: The demo pre-flight now shows on screen before the shifts, with your own demo client to set up before Shift 1. Shift 2 has a pay and team-meeting rehearsal, the Square step checks the trainer's own phone and Tap to Pay, habit and goal practice is a spoken role-play, each trainer's sheet has a confidence record, and there's a new-trainer launch running order with owners.

already_right.title: Your training order
already_right.text: Ava before app setup; four four-hour shifts, a course pass and your practical sign-off before coaching alone. Your four shift focus areas stay.

already_right.title: Selling and booking basics
already_right.text: Book all three Kickstart sessions where possible before payment. Start the recap and offer at minute 22. Thinking time does not require a discount.

already_right.title: Program and check-in rhythm
already_right.text: Three-week Kickstart programs; six weeks is the ongoing refresh default. Repeat bookings stay flexible. Check-ins happen during a rest or at the end.

already_right.title: Safety ownership
already_right.text: Urgent matters are a call to you; call 000 first in an emergency. You approve return to exercise. Clinical facts stay on JF Notes with you tagged directly.

already_right.title: Support and money ownership
already_right.text: Ava first for everyday help. You confirm spares, receive payment-change tasks, handle JF+ and Game Plans, and rehearse sales with trainers who need help. Trainers stay for forfeited slots.

already_right.title: The tools already in place
already_right.text: The narrowed certificate rules and app upload, incident follow-up task, Friday session sign-off, manager lesson unlock and current-program default stay. Old tools stay retired.

open.title: Some shift topics stay as your method
open.text: The guide keeps all 23 discussion topics in your wording, with today's rule printed beside each one. It doesn't invent methods where your notes are brief, so add detail any time.

open.title: Some demo actions stay in the course
open.text: The practice account is for ordinary 1:1 booking practice. Free-session, Kickstart, Strategy and payment practice stay in the course simulations.

open.title: Printable sheets don't save progress
open.text: Print one observation sheet per trainer. Ticks, observations and signatures stay on paper; they aren't stored in the Playbook.

open.title: Separate from this update
open.text: The free-session invitation email, appointments exactly at the notice cut-off and payroll rules weren't changed. App feature requests outside onboarding stay separate.

closing: Thanks for working through it, Gab. Your wording and your training shifts are at the centre of this update.
